headings.text: How Trump's commerce secretary cultivated Nvidia's CEO while chip controls slipped

firstImages.alt: Iran displays its military arsenal, including ballistic and hypersonic missiles, unmanned aerial vehicles, satellite launch vehicles and air defense systems, in the capital Tehran, Iran.

Mourners attend the funeral of Samir Abu Younis, a senior Hamas commander who was killed in an Israeli airstrike, according to medics, at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, in the southern Gaza Strip, November 15, 2026.

US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, left, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, right speak in the Cross Hall of the White House before an event on "Investing in America" on April 30, 2025. Trump was joined by CEOs to highlight companies and their investments in the United States during the event.

The Washington Monument seen in the distance as passengers and planes wait at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA), in Arlington, Virginia, just outside Washington, DC, on November 14, 2026. Flights in the United States are resuming on Saturday after being grounded for several hours due to a major communications outage on November 13, though authorities said returning to normal operations would take time. Friday's nationwide ground stop sparked widespread chaos and left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before departure by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events.

A plane takes off over the control tower at Washington Dulles International Airport in Chantilly, Virginia, after the Federal Aviation Administration lifted a nationwide ground stop, on Saturday, November 14.
